transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

Running a microwave empty is hard on the magnetron and can easily overheat internal parts. The "horrible smell" usually comes from burnt dust, a scorched waveguide cover (the small flat panel inside), or melted plastic components like the turntable motor casing. To see if it's just a smell issue or actual damage: with the microwave unplugged and cool, check the small rectangular cover on the inner wall. If it is blackened or holed, that needs replacing. Also, did you see any sparking while it was running? Please let me know what you see inside and if there was any arcing.

There was some smoke coming out of the vents at the side when we opened the door, plus a hot electrical burnt smell. I didn't see any sparking. It's turned off at the switch but still plugged in - is it safe, or should I just bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If there are flames or smoke is still coming from it, keep away, don't open the door of an oven, microwave or dryer that is on fire, switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.

candidates.cause: Burnt waveguide cover or internal contamination from arcing/overheating
Smell from overheated plastic components (turntable motor, light bulb casing)
Magnetron damage due to prolonged no-load operation
